t:
Section 508(a) of the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1508(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

“(7) Adequate coverage for states.—

“(A) Definition of adequately served.—In this paragraph, the term ‘adequately served’ means having a participation rate that is at least 50 percent of the national average participation rate.
“(B) Review.—The Board shall review the policies and plans of insurance that are offered by approved insurance providers under this title to determine if each State is adequately served by the policies and plans of insurance.
“(C) Report.—
“(i) In general.—Not later than 30 days after completion of the review under subparagraph (B), the Board shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the review.
“(ii) Recommendations.—The report shall include recommendations to increase participation in States that are not adequately served by the policies and plans of insurance.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "participation rate" and "recommendations to increase participation" signal public participation, but those phrases refer to enrollment in crop insurance, not involvement in a federal decision. The only process here is an internal review by the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation's Board followed by a report to Congress, which stays inside the federal government. No comment period, hearing, rulemaking, right to sue, or consultation with states or other outside parties is required.
fable.s: the Board shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the review.

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Board to submit a report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The mention of 'participation rate' refers to farmers' enrollment in insurance programs, which is an application/benefit mechanism, not a process for outside parties to consult with the government on decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Not later than 30 days after completion of the review under subparagraph (B), the Board shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the review.

opus.w: The section has a federal Board review insurance coverage and report its findings and recommendations to Congress, so every actor is inside the federal government. "Participation" here means enrollment rates in crop insurance, not outside parties being consulted in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, or consultation with states.
opus.s: the Board shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the review.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the word "participation" appears several times. But here it means farmers buying crop insurance (the "participation rate"), not outsiders taking part in a federal decision. The Board is the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation's board, which is part of the federal government. It reviews insurance policies on its own and reports to Congress, which is also inside the government. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Federal Crop Insurance Board (a federal entity) to review insurance policies and submit a report to Congress (another federal entity). The term 'participation' refers to the enrollment rate of farmers in insurance programs, not to a process of public consultation or coordination with outside parties. Since all actors involved in the decision-making and reporting process (the Board and Congress) are inside the federal government, this does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: The Board shall review the policies and plans of insurance that are offered by approved insurance providers under this title to determine if each State is adequately served by the policies and plans of insurance. ... The Board shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the review.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The text mentions "participation rate" and "increase participation," which might suggest that the section involves public participation in a decision-making process. However, "participation" here refers to farmers enrolling in crop insurance programs, not to outside parties consulting with the government on policy decisions. The section describes an internal review by the Federal Crop Insurance Board and a report to Congress. Both the Board and Congress are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for the government to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities before making a decision. The report is submitted *to* Congress, which is a trap (reports to Congress are not participation).
